'''George William Whitehead, Jr.''' (August 2, 1918 – April 12, 2004) was an American professor of mathematics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]], and a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]. He is known for his work on [[algebraic topology]].<ref name="mit">{{cite news| url=https://news.mit.edu/2004/whitehead-0428 | title=George Whitehead dies at 85 | date=April 28, 2004 |work=MIT Tech Talk | publisher=[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] | access-date=October 25, 2025 }}</ref> He invented the [[J-homomorphism]], and was among the first to systematically calculate the [[homotopy groups of spheres]]. He is also central to the study of [[stable homotopy theory]], in particular making concrete the connections between [[Spectrum (topology)|spectra]] and [[Cohomology#Axioms and generalized cohomology theories|generalized homology/cohomology theories]].<ref name="adams">{{cite book |last1=Adams |first1=Frank |title=Stable Homotopy and Generalized Homology |date=1974 |publisher=[[The University of Chicago Press]] |pages=196–214}}</ref>

Whitehead was born in [[Bloomington, Illinois]], and received his Ph.D. in mathematics from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1941, under the supervision of [[Norman Steenrod]].<ref name="mit" /> After teaching at [[Purdue University]], [[Princeton University]], and [[Brown University]], he took a position at MIT in 1949, where he remained until his retirement in 1985. He advised 13 Ph.D. students, including [[Robert Aumann]], [[Edgar Brown, Jr.]], and [[John Coleman Moore]], and has over 1,940 [[academic genealogy|academic descendants]] (as of 2025).<ref>{{mathgenealogy|6374}}</ref>

He was a member of the [[American Academy of Arts & Sciences]] (elected in 1954)<ref name="amacad">{{cite web| url=https://www.amacad.org/person/george-william-whitehead | title=Professor George William Whitehead (1918–2004) | publisher=[[American Academy of Arts & Sciences]] | date=Apr 2025 | access-date=October 25, 2025 }}</ref> and the United States [[National Academy of Sciences]] (elected in 1972).<ref name="nasonline">{{cite web| url=https://www.nasonline.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/whitehead-george.pdf | title=George W. Whitehead Jr. 1918–2004 | first=Haynes R. | last=Miller | author-link=Haynes R. Miller | series=Biographical Memoirs| publisher=[[National Academy of Sciences]] | date=2015 | access-date=23 November 2015 | url-status=live | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151123120044/http://www.nasonline.org/publications/biographical-memoirs/memoir-pdfs/whitehead-george.pdf | archive-date=23 November 2015 }}</ref>
